CONTINUITY LOCK: A single continuous fixed-camera shot in the natural pre-capture moonlit mountain jungle. Preserve exactly the starting image creature identities, markings, anatomy, scale and illustration style: rich vintage comic ink, dense crosshatching, cool teal night and copper-gold highlights. Exactly two creatures throughout. Rigid consistent rock and tree landmarks. No enclosure, buildings, artificial lights, captions, audio, cuts, camera moves, morphing, duplication or teleportation. This is a tense survival encounter, not friendly play. One decisive readable near miss, no contact, catching, injury or gore. Physical continuous movement, claws and feet supported when grounded. Both opponents remain readable until the escape, with no aimless wandering.

FIVE SECONDS. CRITICAL PHYSICAL ACTION: the bat-plesiosaur is airborne and MUST actively flap BOTH large wings continuously throughout the entire shot, including while looking down and after the rabbit escapes. Strong obvious full downstrokes and upstrokes from shoulder joints, flexible elbow joints, membranes changing silhouette, tips sweeping clearly above then below the body. About two wingbeats per second; never frozen outstretched wings, never static hovering or gliding. Slight rhythmic body lift on every downstroke. Wings keep flapping independently of the head and neck motion. Feet remain airborne.
Exactly one rabbit-moth starts left of the bat. 0-0.6sec: immediate visible powered wingbeats by the predator; rabbit flies briefly left above the fallen branch. 0.6-1.4sec: rabbit makes ONE decisive down-left dive BEHIND and UNDER the fallen branch to escape. Bat extends long furry neck and snaps at the rabbit's FORMER position, a narrow but clear miss. Rabbit stays visibly separated from mouth, never enters or touches jaws. The rabbit passes progressively behind the solid branch by real occlusion. By1.5sec the whole rabbit including ears and wings is hidden beneath the branch and leaving down-left.
1.5-5sec: rabbit remains completely offscreen or concealed beneath branch, NEVER comes back up, NEVER reappears in its original spot, no second rabbit. Bat brakes with vigorous flapping, retracts neck and peers down at the empty branch while CONTINUING FULL WINGBEATS. Predator stays mostly right half of frame, no wandering. Empty hiding place remains empty. Keep powerful wing cycle going to the final frame. Rabbit's identity and graceful fast evasive dive from original reference retained. Do not perch: this is visibly powered flight.
